**Grant Application: CalVIP Funding Request**

Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC), a minority-owned social enterprise, seeks a CalVIP grant of up to $500,000 to tackle the urgent need for gun violence prevention and safety education in Sacramento’s communities of color. These neighborhoods face disproportionately high risks of accidental firearm incidents due to lack of awareness and safe handling practices. Our mission is to empower these communities with vital knowledge through innovative, culturally resonant programs.

Our unique approach includes the "Gloxsie 21" cartoon IP, delivering age-appropriate gun safety messages to youth in an engaging format. We pair this with AI education, empowering young people to develop their own safety content, fostering digital literacy and future-proof skills. Hands-on community workshops, co-hosted with our trusted partner Church of Legacy, reinforce practical safety protocols, including secure storage and responsible firearm interactions for all ages.

Anticipated outcomes include a measurable increase in safe gun storage practices, reduced accidental firearm injuries, enhanced community-wide safety awareness, and youth empowerment through technological literacy. GAFC is uniquely qualified as a minority-owned organization with deep roots and authentic understanding of the communities we serve. Our provocative name sparks essential conversations, while our innovative blend of education, entertainment, and technology, coupled with Church of Legacy’s trusted reach, ensures maximum impact. This CalVIP grant will allow us to scale these vital, culturally relevant programs, fostering lasting safety and positive community transformation.
